title: Wolves Down The Waterfall
mainIdea: Struggle to stay alive / Heroic act

vocabulary.definition: An action to hurt or harm someone aggressively
It is a condition when something goes extremely bad
It is a cold season in subtropical zones when the snow falls down
A steep and high area of a rock at the edge of a land or river
A land along the side of a river that can be stepped on

passage: During a terrible winter in the northern mountains, a young explorer named Arthur found himself trapped near the riverbank. The temperature had dropped well below freezing, and the snow was falling heavily. As he looked up, he saw a pack of wolves preparing to attack from the high cliff above. Realizing the danger, Arthur had to act quickly. He slid down the steep bank, barely holding onto the icy rocks. In a heroic struggle to stay alive, he crossed the freezing waterfall just as the wolves reached the edge. His brave actions saved him from what could have been a fatal encounter on that cold, unforgiving night.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The migration patterns of wolves in winter
A struggle to stay alive and a heroic escape from danger
How to navigate freezing mountain waterfalls
The geological formation of high river cliffs
questions.answer: A struggle to stay alive and a heroic escape from danger
questions.explanation: The passage highlights Arthur's struggle to stay alive and his brave escape across the freezing waterfall to avoid the wolves.

questions.question: What does the word 'cliff' mean in this context?
options: A sandy beach along the ocean
A small wooden bridge over a stream
A steep and high area of rock at the edge of land
A shallow part of a river bed
questions.answer: A steep and high area of rock at the edge of land
questions.explanation: According to the vocabulary and context, a cliff is a steep and high rocky area at the edge of land.

questions.question: Where did Arthur slide down to escape the wolves?
options: Into a deep dark cave
Down the steep bank of the river
Up to the top of the cliff
Onto a highway nearby
questions.answer: Down the steep bank of the river
questions.explanation: The passage states that Arthur 'slid down the steep bank' of the river to escape.

title: The Story of Potato

vocabulary.definition: A group of people who are from Spain
It's a weather condition of an area in a period of time
A layer of earth in which plants grow
A bad condition when something/someone is being infected and made unhealthy
An action to construct or build something

passage: In the sixteenth century, the Spaniards returned from South America with a strange new plant: the potato. At first, Europeans were skeptical of this tuber. However, they soon realized that the local climate was perfect for it, and the rich soil allowed potatoes to grow in abundance. When a severe disease destroyed other grain crops, the potato kept populations from starving. Landowners began to put up new storage warehouses to protect their potato harvests. Through agricultural adaptation and immigration of ideas, the potato transitioned from an exotic curiosity into Europe's most vital food source.

questions.question: Who originally brought the potato to Europe?
options: French merchants
The Spaniards
English sailors
German farmers
questions.answer: The Spaniards
questions.explanation: The passage mentions that the Spaniards returned from South America with the potato plant in the sixteenth century.

questions.question: Why did landowners 'put up' new warehouses?
options: To sell them to immigrants
To house their agricultural workers
To protect and store their potato harvests
To protect themselves from diseases
questions.answer: To protect and store their potato harvests
questions.explanation: The passage states that landowners began to 'put up' (construct) storage warehouses to protect their potato harvests.

questions.question: Which factor made Europe suitable for growing potatoes?
options: The expensive importing services
The favorable climate and rich soil
A lack of crop diseases
Special chemicals used by Spaniards
questions.answer: The favorable climate and rich soil
questions.explanation: The passage highlights that the 'local climate was perfect' and the 'rich soil allowed potatoes to grow in abundance'.

title: Venice and Its Canals

vocabulary.definition: A waterway for traffic in Venice
A person who drives a gondola in Venice
A feeling of embarrassment of being poor or doing something wrong
A tool that is used to row water so the boat can be moved
A thing that is given to people who are worth it / appreciation for effort

passage: Venice is famous worldwide for its beautiful canals, which serve as the city's main highways. A skilled gondolier guides each traditional boat through these narrow water channels. One day, a young gondolier lost his heavy wooden oar in the canal, which made him feel ashamed because he could not afford to buy a new one immediately. Observing his distress, a generous tourist offered to buy him a replacement. In return, the gondolier offered the tourist a free private tour of the hidden waterways, which was the best reward the tourist could have received for his kindness.

questions.question: What is a 'gondolier'?
options: A type of Venetian house built on water
A person who steers a gondola boat
A local police officer in Venice
A tool used to clean the canals
questions.answer: A person who steers a gondola boat
questions.explanation: A gondolier is defined as a person who drives or steers a gondola in Venice.

questions.question: Why did the gondolier feel ashamed?
options: He crashed into another gondola
He forgot the history of Venice
He lost his oar and could not afford to buy a new one
He charged the tourist too much money
questions.answer: He lost his oar and could not afford to buy a new one
questions.explanation: The passage says losing his oar made him feel ashamed because he was too poor to buy a replacement.

questions.question: What reward did the gondolier give the tourist?
options: A sum of money
A beautiful painted oar
A free private tour of the hidden waterways
A delicious Venetian dinner
questions.answer: A free private tour of the hidden waterways
questions.explanation: The passage mentions that the gondolier rewarded the tourist's kindness with a free tour of the canals.

title: A Walk in the School Yard

vocabulary.definition: Damaged to the point of being no longer usable
The underside of a piece of footwear
The back part of the human foot below the ankle, or the raised back part of a shoe
A thing of great significance or value
A large area of a school where students play sports or do activities

passage: Lukas loved running around the school yard during recess. However, his favorite leather shoes were completely worn out. The soles had split open, and the heels were loose, making it difficult for him to run safely. His teacher noticed Lukas tripping and reminded him that taking care of his feet is important for his health. Lukas took the shoes to a local cobbler, who repaired both the soles and heels. The next day, Lukas returned to the school yard, running faster than ever in his newly restored shoes.

questions.question: What was wrong with Lukas's shoes?
options: They were too small for him
They were worn out, with split soles and loose heels
They were dirty and needed polish
They were lost in the school yard
questions.answer: They were worn out, with split soles and loose heels
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that Lukas's shoes were worn out, with split soles and loose heels.

questions.question: What is the 'school yard' used for?
options: Taking formal exams
Repairing worn out shoes
Recess, playing sports, and school activities
Selling leather products
questions.answer: Recess, playing sports, and school activities
questions.explanation: The school yard is described as the area where students run around and play sports during recess.

questions.question: What advice did the teacher give Lukas?
options: To buy brand new designer shoes
That taking care of his feet is important for health
To stop running during recess
To become a cobbler
questions.answer: That taking care of his feet is important for health
questions.explanation: The teacher reminded Lukas that taking care of his feet is important.

title: The Forgotten Code

vocabulary.definition: A device for human tasks or for working
A feeling of not being able to do anything
A certain way to do something procedurally
A sign or system of letters/symbols to communicate with others
A short note sent to other people for communicating

passage: When the ship's communication transmitter broke down, the crew felt helpless. They were miles out at sea with no way to call for help. The captain realized they needed a different tool to communicate. He suggested using a mirror to flash a distress signal in Morse code towards a distant lighthouse. This method of communication was outdated but reliable. Within minutes, they sent a message using light flashes. Soon, the lighthouse responder spotted the signal and sent back a message indicating that a rescue boat was on its way.

questions.question: Why did the ship's crew feel helpless?
options: They ran out of food and water
The transmitter broke down and they couldn't call for help
They did not know how to steer the ship
The lighthouse was closed for the night
questions.answer: The transmitter broke down and they couldn't call for help
questions.explanation: The passage notes that they felt helpless because the transmitter broke, leaving them with no way to call for help.

questions.question: What alternative tool did they use to send a signal?
options: A cell phone
A mirror to flash Morse code
A megaphone to shout
A long wooden oar
questions.answer: A mirror to flash Morse code
questions.explanation: The captain suggested using a mirror to flash Morse code as an alternative communication tool.

questions.question: What was the result of their Morse code method?
options: The mirror fell into the ocean
They received a message that rescue was coming
The lighthouse did not see the signal
They repaired the broken transmitter
questions.answer: They received a message that rescue was coming
questions.explanation: The lighthouse responder saw the flashes and sent back a message saying a rescue boat was on its way.

title: On Board the Merchant Ship

vocabulary.definition: An action of being on a ship/vehicle; or improving knowledge of employees
Horizontal supports for the structure of a building or ship
An action we do in a particular way
A tall cupboard made of metal used to keep things safe
A painful sensation in the head

passage: As soon as the new crew came on board, they were briefed on safety rules. The heavy wooden beams supporting the ship's ceiling were low, so everyone had to watch their head. The first mate warned the crew to behave responsibly, especially during rough weather, and to store all personal gear in their designated lockers. Later that night, a strong storm hit the ship. The constant rocking gave the captain a severe headache, but thanks to the crew's excellent behavior, all supplies remained locked and safe.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'on board' in this passage?
options: Writing notes on a chalkboard
Being inside or on a ship/vehicle
Getting bored of ship duties
Improving knowledge of employees
questions.answer: Being inside or on a ship/vehicle
questions.explanation: In this context, 'on board' refers to being on the merchant ship.

questions.question: Why did the captain get a headache?
options: He bumped his head on the wooden beams
He was stressed about losing a locker key
The constant rocking of the ship during the storm
The crew refused to behave responsibly
questions.answer: The constant rocking of the ship during the storm
questions.explanation: The passage says that the storm's constant rocking gave the captain a severe headache.

questions.question: Where were the crew instructed to store their gear?
options: On top of the wooden beams
In their designated lockers
On the deck of the ship
With the captain
questions.answer: In their designated lockers
questions.explanation: The crew was warned to store all personal gear in their designated lockers.

title: Mowing the Lawn

vocabulary.definition: An activity to cut down grass with a machine
A cylinder-shaped tool for rolling something like cable or hose
A situation when something is overbalanced and turns over
An amusing incident that makes people laugh
An action that causes someone or something to fall without control

passage: Uncle Bob was mowing the grass yesterday using a heavy lawnmower. He was pulling a long extension cord from a plastic reel. While walking backward near the garden slope, the reel tipped over. Uncle Bob tripped on the cord, tumbled down the grass, and landed directly in a pile of soft autumn leaves. Although it looked painful, Uncle Bob sat up and burst out laughing at how funny he must have looked. The lawn was cut, and he walked away with nothing but a little dirt on his shirt.

questions.question: What was Uncle Bob doing at the start of the passage?
options: Mowing the grass with a lawnmower
Raking autumn leaves into piles
Rolling a plastic cable reel
Buying a new garden machine
questions.answer: Mowing the grass with a lawnmower
questions.explanation: The passage begins by stating that Uncle Bob was mowing the grass using a lawnmower.

questions.question: What caused Uncle Bob to tumble down the grass?
options: A sudden gust of heavy wind
The lawnmower broke and exploded
He tripped on the extension cord after the reel tipped over
He fell asleep while walking
questions.answer: He tripped on the extension cord after the reel tipped over
questions.explanation: The passage notes that the reel tipped over, and Uncle Bob tripped on the cord and tumbled down.

questions.question: How did Uncle Bob react to his fall?
options: He got angry and cried
He blamed the lawnmower manufacturer
He laughed because he found the incident funny
He went to the hospital for a headache
questions.answer: He laughed because he found the incident funny
questions.explanation: The passage says Uncle Bob burst out laughing at how funny he must have looked.

title: The Woodcutter's Balance

vocabulary.definition: A hunted animal targeted by a predator
An activity to swing or dash something quickly
An accident when someone is unable to remain upright and steady
A sharp tool used to cut wood
A condition when someone loses consciousness suddenly due to lack of oxygen

passage: Deep in the forest, a woodcutter named Sean was chopping old pine trees. He raised his heavy iron axe and swung it with all his strength. Suddenly, he heard a rustling sound and saw a wolf chasing its prey nearby. Distracted by the wild scene, Sean lost his balance on the slippery mud. He fell hard, hitting his leg against a tree root. The sudden pain was so intense that Sean fainted. When he woke up an hour later, the animals were gone, and he carefully used his axe as a walking stick to hobble back to his cabin.

questions.question: What distracted Sean while he was chopping wood?
options: A heavy rainstorm starting
A wolf chasing its prey
He lost his heavy iron axe
A loud sound from a distant cabin
questions.answer: A wolf chasing its prey
questions.explanation: Sean was distracted when he saw a wolf chasing its prey nearby.

questions.question: Why did Sean faint?
options: He was extremely hungry and tired
He saw a scary wolf coming to attack him
He fell and hit his leg, causing intense pain
He ran out of oxygen inside the forest cabin
questions.answer: He fell and hit his leg, causing intense pain
questions.explanation: The passage states that the sudden pain from hitting his leg was so intense that Sean fainted.

questions.question: What tool did Sean use to chop wood?
options: A hand saw
An iron axe
A wooden spade
A heavy hammer
questions.answer: An iron axe
questions.explanation: The passage mentions that Sean was chopping trees with a heavy iron axe.

title: The Strange Pedlar

vocabulary.definition: A person who goes from place to place selling small items
Something unusual or difficult to understand
Something that is very valuable or represents great wealth
A tool used for digging soil or sand with a long handle
A large box made of wood for storing goods, or the upper front of the body

passage: A strange pedlar arrived in our village yesterday, carrying unusual trinkets from distant lands. Instead of selling jewelry or cloth, he claimed to possess a map leading to a buried treasure. A young villager named Leo decided to buy the map. Armed with a rusty spade, Leo walked to the old oak tree marked on the map and began to dig. After hours of hard work, his spade struck something solid. It was a large wooden chest. Leo opened it and found ancient coins and silver plates, proving that the strange pedlar's map was genuine.

questions.question: What did the pedlar sell to Leo?
options: A large wooden chest
A map to buried treasure
A rusty digging spade
Ancient coins and jewelry
questions.answer: A map to buried treasure
questions.explanation: The passage states that the pedlar claimed to have a map to buried treasure, which Leo bought.

questions.question: What tool did Leo use to dig up the treasure?
options: A wooden axe
A spade
A pickaxe
An iron oar
questions.answer: A spade
questions.explanation: Leo dug up the chest using a rusty spade.

questions.question: Where was the chest buried?
options: Under the village market
In the pedlar's backyard
Under the old oak tree
Near the waterfall
questions.answer: Under the old oak tree
questions.explanation: Leo went to the 'old oak tree' marked on the map and digged there.

title: An Honest Return

vocabulary.definition: To slide accidentally or move from a correct place without intending to
Truthful, sincere, or able to be trusted
A condition of something that is not special or is usual to look at
A condition of wanting more than enough of something, especially money or food
To behave as if something is true when it is not

passage: While walking through the crowded market, an ordinary man named Philip noticed that a wealthy merchant's wallet had slipped out of his pocket and fallen onto the cobblestones. Philip picked it up and saw it was full of high-value bills. For a moment, a greedy thought crossed his mind to keep the cash. However, Philip was an honest man. He caught up to the merchant and returned the wallet. The merchant was so grateful that he offered Philip a reward. Philip pretended he didn't need the money, but the merchant insisted on thanking him with a generous gift.

questions.question: What happened to the merchant's wallet?
options: It was stolen by a greedy thief
It slipped out of his pocket and fell to the ground
Philip sold it to the merchant
It was buried under the market soil
questions.answer: It slipped out of his pocket and fell to the ground
questions.explanation: The passage says the wallet 'had slipped out of his pocket and fallen onto the cobblestones'.

questions.question: Why did Philip return the wallet?
options: Because he was an honest man
Because the wallet was empty
Because the police was watching him
Because he was greedy
questions.answer: Because he was an honest man
questions.explanation: Philip returned the wallet because he was an honest man, despite a brief greedy thought.

questions.question: What did Philip do when the merchant offered him a reward?
options: He took all the money greedily
He ran away immediately without speaking
He pretended he didn't need the money
He asked for a job at the merchant's shop
questions.answer: He pretended he didn't need the money
questions.explanation: The passage states that Philip 'pretended he didn't need the money' before the merchant insisted.

title: The Selfish Wish

vocabulary.definition: Caring only for oneself without consideration for others
Allowed, approved, or assumed to be true
To go missing, vanish, or become impossible to find
Two people who are in a relationship, or a few things that are similar
Right away, without thinking or waiting

passage: In a small cottage, a young couple lived near an ancient wishing well. One evening, the husband made a selfish wish for a bag of gold, wishing only for his own luxury without thinking of his wife. The well granted his wish immediately, and a heavy bag of gold appeared on the table. However, as soon as he touched it, his wife began to disappear. Horrified, he realized the price of his greed. He rushed back to the well and begged for his wife's return, offering to make the gold vanish. Fortunately, the well listened, his wife returned, and the gold was gone forever.

questions.question: What was selfish about the husband's wish?
options: He wished for a giant wolf to attack the village
He wished for gold only for himself, ignoring his wife
He wished to leave his cottage immediately
He did not want to share his food with the couple next door
questions.answer: He wished for gold only for himself, ignoring his wife
questions.explanation: The passage explains the wish was selfish because he wished only for his own luxury without thinking of his wife.

questions.question: What happened immediately after the wish was granted?
options: A bag of gold appeared on the table
The cottage caught fire
His wife disappeared
The well dried up
questions.answer: A bag of gold appeared on the table
questions.explanation: The well granted his wish immediately, causing a bag of gold to appear on the table.

questions.question: What did the husband do when his wife began to disappear?
options: He bought a new house with the gold
He pretended nothing was wrong
He returned to the well to beg for his wife's return
He ran away to another country
questions.answer: He returned to the well to beg for his wife's return
questions.explanation: When his wife began to disappear, he rushed back to the well and begged for her return.

title: The Lazy Team

vocabulary.definition: A condition when a person has no willingness to work or use any effort
A body part between the chest and legs; the stomach
Able to be depended on or deserving of trust
A number of people who do something together as a group
Something given in exchange for good behavior or good work

passage: In a local village, a team of builders was hired to construct a new community bridge. Most of the workers were lazy, spending their afternoons sleeping under trees with full bellies instead of working. Only their supervisor, a trusted man named Thomas, worked hard every day. When the project owner visited, he saw that the bridge was incomplete. He decided that only Thomas deserved the bonus reward. The lazy team members complained, but the owner made it clear that rewards are only given to those who put in the effort.

questions.question: Why did the bridge project take so long?
options: The team had no tools to dig the soil
Most of the workers were lazy and slept instead of working
Thomas did not know how to build a bridge
A severe disease infected the whole team
questions.answer: Most of the workers were lazy and slept instead of working
questions.explanation: The passage notes that most workers were lazy, sleeping under trees instead of working.

questions.question: Why was Thomas the only one who received a reward?
options: He was the owner's relative
He was a trusted supervisor who worked hard while others slaked off
He spent the money to feed the lazy workers
He bought the materials with his own money
questions.answer: He was a trusted supervisor who worked hard while others slaked off
questions.explanation: Thomas was rewarded because he was trusted and worked hard, unlike the lazy team members.

questions.question: What does the word 'belly' refer to in the passage?
options: A tool used to lift heavy beams
The supervisor's storage locker
The stomach, showing the workers had eaten and slept
The support base of the bridge
questions.answer: The stomach, showing the workers had eaten and slept
questions.explanation: The workers slept with 'full bellies', referring to their stomachs after eating.

title: Crawling for Crumbs
mainIdea: Hunger and survival in the wilderness

vocabulary.definition: An activity of moving on hands and knees close to the ground
A feeling of needing food
An area of land that has territory and its own government, or rural countryside
A small meal eaten in the late evening
Small pieces that have fallen from bread, cookies, or cake

passage: An old traveller was walking through the open country when he lost his backpack. By nightfall, he was freezing and extremely hungry. He saw a tiny light in the distance and crawled towards it on his hands and knees. The light belonged to a small cottage. An old woman opened the door and invited him in for a warm supper. Although the meal was simple bread and soup, the traveller was so grateful that he carefully ate every single bite, leaving not even a few crumbs on the wooden table.

questions.question: How did the traveller move toward the cottage light?
options: He rode a horse across the country
He crawled on his hands and knees
He ran as fast as he could
He floated down the river
questions.answer: He crawled on his hands and knees
questions.explanation: The passage states that the traveller 'crawled towards it on his hands and knees'.

questions.question: What did the old woman offer the traveller?
options: A map to a buried chest of gold
A new backpack with tools
A warm supper of bread and soup
A ride to the nearest country
questions.answer: A warm supper of bread and soup
questions.explanation: The old woman invited the traveller in for a warm 'supper' of bread and soup.

questions.question: Why did the traveller leave no crumbs?
options: The old woman scolded him for being messy
He was extremely hungry and grateful for the food
The crumbs fell into his boots
The bread was too soft to make crumbs
questions.answer: He was extremely hungry and grateful for the food
questions.explanation: He was so hungry and grateful that he ate every bite, leaving no crumbs.

title: Beside the Fireplace

vocabulary.definition: A space in the wall of a room for making the room warmer with fire
A long ribbon or thin rope to tie something valuable
A device for measuring and showing time on a wall or table
A small sharp organ of insects (like bees) that causes pain/injury
A sleeveless outer garment worn to cover someone

passage: After spending all afternoon in the forest collecting honey, Daniel returned to his cabin. He was suffering from several painful bee stings on his hands. He immediately lit a fire in the fireplace to warm up the chilly room. He hung his heavy wool cloak on the wall hook next to the ticking clock. To soothe his stings, he wrapped his hands in a cool damp cloth, tying it securely with a piece of cotton cord. Resting by the fire, Daniel watched the clock hands move, feeling the warmth slowly take away the sharp pain of the day.

questions.question: Why did Daniel light a fire in the fireplace?
options: To cook a large supper of wild prey
To warm up the chilly cabin room
To burn his old wool cloak
To smoke out the bees in the forest
questions.answer: To warm up the chilly cabin room
questions.explanation: Daniel lit the fireplace 'to warm up the chilly room' after returning from the forest.

questions.question: What injured Daniel during his honey collection?
options: He got caught in a cotton cord
He was bitten by a wolf on the bank
Several painful bee stings on his hands
He bumped his head on ship beams
questions.answer: Several painful bee stings on his hands
questions.explanation: The passage notes that Daniel was suffering from several painful bee stings.

questions.question: What did Daniel hang next to the clock?
options: A cotton cord
His heavy wool cloak
His beehive tools
A damp cloth wrapper
questions.answer: His heavy wool cloak
questions.explanation: The passage states that he hung his heavy wool cloak on the wall hook next to the ticking clock.

title: The Candy Counter

vocabulary.definition: A long passage in a building with rooms or seats on both sides
A behavior toward someone, or an enjoyable special gift/food
A clay-like material used by children for play and modeling
A long flat table in a shop for serving customers
A hard, chewy candy made from boiled sugar and butter

passage: Walking down the school corridor, young Sally was excited. It was Friday, which meant she could buy a special sweet treat at the local store. She hurried inside and walked up to the glass counter. Behind it stood jars of delicious, chewy toffees and colorful lollipops. As she paid the cashier, Sally noticed a small box of plasticine modeling clay on the side shelf, reminding her of art class. With her sweet toffees in one hand and her art clay in the other, she walked home happily, enjoying the perfect end to her school week.

options: A notebook for her art class
Some chewy toffees
A new wool cloak
A clock for the corridor
questions.answer: Some chewy toffees
questions.explanation: The passage mentions that she walked up to the counter and bought chewy toffees.

questions.question: What is 'plasticine' used for in the passage?
options: It is a hard chewy sweet candy
A cleaning tool for the school corridor
Modeling clay for children's play/art
Tying packages on the counter
questions.answer: Modeling clay for children's play/art
questions.explanation: Plasticine is defined as a clay-like material used by children for play and modeling.

questions.question: Where did Sally walk before entering the candy store?
options: Down the school corridor
Along the freezing riverbank
Through the open forest country
On board a large merchant ship
questions.answer: Down the school corridor
questions.explanation: The passage begins with Sally 'walking down the school corridor'.
